candidates.title: Deferred domain loading for CLI startup
candidates.source: Every atlas invocation costs ~0.50 s before it does anything: ~346 ms importing atlas_agent.cli, ~75 ms building the argparse tree, ~12 ms interpreter startup. The suite spawns the CLI from 97 call sites, and the dev gate's slowest step spends 73% of its wall clock in 21 such subprocesses, so this is primarily a developer-loop cost rather than a UX one.
candidates.acceptance_criteria: A measured reduction in atlas --version wall time with the command surface unchanged: scripts/check_cli_command_compatibility.py passes, every trust-contract envelope is byte-identical, and a test pins the reduction so it cannot silently regress.
candidates.safety_notes: Import-timing and packaging only. Changes no gate, no default, and no runtime decision: not RiskManager, approval queues, kill switch, heartbeat, deadman, the audit hash-chain, live-submit opt-in, or can_submit. Loads no credentials and adds no network access. The cli_bootstrap.py pre-router keeps its four configless commands and its stdlib-only module scope.
candidates.open_question: Two levers, priced in docs/development/safety-invariant-audit-followups.md. ConfigDict(defer_build=True) measures 74% off pydantic class creation (200 synthetic models: 178 ms to 46.5 ms), about a quarter of startup, but 128 of 129 model classes inherit BaseModel directly with no shared base, and it moves a malformed model from an import-time error to a first-use error. Lazy per-domain handler import has a larger ceiling (config alone imports in 137 ms against 273 ms for cli_commands) but threads local imports through a 5.9k-line dispatch whose command surface is a pinned trust contract. Deciding which, or neither, is the candidate.

candidates.title: Wire the declared daily-loss and leverage limits
candidates.source: Hard invariant 5 states RiskManager enforces limits on position size, notional, daily loss, exposure, symbols, and leverage. Four are enforced and have rules. Two are not: max_daily_loss_pct is declared in RiskLimits and read by no rule, and OrderRiskInput.leverage is populated on both the paper and live-submit paths and read by no rule. A portfolio 50% down on the day, against a 2% declared limit, evaluates allowed=True with zero violations; so does an order carrying 10x leverage.
candidates.acceptance_criteria: The two xfail cases in tests/risk/test_declared_limits_are_wired.py pass with their markers removed, each new guard is verified by breaking the source and confirming the specific test fails, and no previously accepted order is rejected except by the limit being added.
candidates.safety_notes: Tightens the deterministic risk gate; enables nothing. Adds no live trading, live submit, broker or provider execution, credential loading, or network access, and changes no default toward permissiveness. It can only reject orders that are accepted today.
candidates.open_question: The daily-loss chain is a stub at both ends: realized_pnl_today is carried from PortfolioState through PortfolioSnapshot into every evaluation, and nothing in src/ ever increments it, so it is always zero. Adding the rule alone would be a limit on a number nobody writes. Closing it properly means deciding where realized daily P&L is accounted — the paper broker's fills, the trade journal, or a session boundary the caller resets — which is a portfolio-accounting decision, not a risk-rule one. Leverage is narrower: no broker adapter forwards the field, so the question is whether to reject leveraged orders at the gate or to stop carrying a field the system does not act on.

candidates.title: Map the research error codes the CLI flattens to a generic message
candidates.source: safe_research_session_error maps a ResearchSessionError to a vetted status and falls back to ('research_error', 'Research command failed.') for anything unrecognised. src/atlas_agent raises 205 distinct literal codes and RESEARCH_SESSION_ERROR_CODES maps 69 of them, so at least 136 land on the generic message. Measured over the CLI, 30 of the 175 atlas research subcommands answer a nonexistent id with 'Research command failed.' while the reason was known, static, and safe to show — for example provider_safety_dossier_source_seal_missing. A further 33 raise sites build their code at runtime and are not counted, so 136 is a lower bound.
candidates.acceptance_criteria: Entries added for the codes an operator can reach, the ratchet in tests/research/test_research_error_code_mapping.py lowered to the new count, and no status string carrying a path, identifier, or any value from the exception rather than a literal.
candidates.safety_notes: The generic fallback stays. It is the fail-safe half of this design — an unmapped exception string must never be echoed, because in general it can carry a path or user data. This only widens the vetted allowlist, so it enables nothing at runtime and changes no gate, default, or trading behaviour.
candidates.open_question: Whether all of them deserve a distinct message, or whether the families collapse into a smaller vocabulary — eleven different not-found spellings already exist across the -show commands (not_found, artifact_not_found, research_artifact_not_found, dossier_not_found, report_not_found, and more). Adding that many strings without deciding the vocabulary first would make the surface harder to consume, not easier.
